mission: Track which foundational historical mathematics works exist, how they can be read today, and how they should be stored locally for ingestion.
storage_rule: Keep raw files outside Git, keep manifests and metadata in Git, and record rights before large-scale ingestion.

sources.title: Rhind Mathematical Papyrus
sources.date_label: circa 1550 BCE manuscript copy of earlier material
sources.significance: Early arithmetic and problem-text tradition for practical computation and geometry.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Pre-proof arithmetic tradition and worked-problem culture.

access_routes.notes: Collection object page for one main Rhind papyrus section with catalog metadata.
Collection object page for the other main Rhind papyrus section.

sources.title: Plimpton 322
sources.date_label: Old Babylonian period, likely 1800 BCE to 1600 BCE
sources.significance: Key artifact for early number systems, tabular computation, and right-triangle relations.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Shows pre-Euclidean numerical structure behind later right-triangle mathematics.

access_routes.notes: Direct catalog route for the tablet with metadata and imaging links.

sources.title: Euclid: Elements
sources.date_label: around 300 BCE; extant through later manuscript and print traditions
sources.significance: Core architecture of axioms, definitions, propositions, and proof dependencies.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Primary anchor for proof culture and the Euclidean form of the Pythagorean theorem.

access_routes.notes: Historical archive with Greek and English material around the Elements.
Useful hub for scanned public-domain editions and lending.

sources.title: Archimedes: The Method and related works
sources.date_label: 3rd century BCE, transmitted through later manuscript traditions
sources.significance: Central for exhaustion methods, geometry, and proto-infinite reasoning.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Essential for the story behind area, volume, and limit-like argumentation.

access_routes.notes: Historical introduction and translated excerpts for The Method.
Hub for scans and editions of The Works of Archimedes.

sources.title: Brahmagupta: Brahmasphutasiddhanta
sources.date_label: 628 CE
sources.significance: Key source for zero, arithmetic rules, and algebraic procedure in the Indian tradition.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for rule-based arithmetic and equation history before later symbolic standardization.

access_routes.notes: Open e-text route to the Sanskrit text based on a historical edition.
Route to Colebrooke-era translation material and later library copies.

sources.title: Algoritmi de numero Indorum
sources.date_label: Latin witness printed in 1857 from the earlier al-Khwarizmi tradition
sources.significance: Important access point for the transmission of Hindu-Arabic numerals and written calculation.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Critical for the story of place-value notation and algorithmic arithmetic.

access_routes.notes: Full-view scan of the 1857 witness edition.

sources.title: Al-Khwarizmi: Algebra of Mohammed ben Musa
sources.date_label: 9th century original; 1831 English translation by Rosen
sources.significance: Anchor text for rhetorical algebra and systematic equation solving.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Essential for the history of quadratic procedures before modern symbolic form.

access_routes.notes: Library hub for Rosen's translation and scan access.
Public scan route that often resolves to the 1831 translation.

sources.title: Fibonacci: Liber Abaci
sources.date_label: 1202, revised 1228
sources.significance: Major transmission route for Hindu-Arabic numerals into Latin Europe.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for arithmetic culture, commercial calculation, and the European adoption story.

access_routes.notes: Digital Liber Abbaci edition and manuscript apparatus through Museo Galileo.
Route to modern translations and library holdings.

sources.title: Newton: The Method of Fluxions and Infinite Series
sources.date_label: written earlier; English publication 1736
sources.significance: Central source for Newtonian calculus language and infinite series methods.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Key for fluxions, fluents, and the connection between changing quantities and integration.

access_routes.notes: Direct public-domain PDF route backed by the Internet Archive scan.
Useful contextual overview of the work and publication history.

sources.title: Leibniz: Nova Methodus pro Maximis et Minimis
sources.significance: Foundational publication for differential notation and the public calculus tradition.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Key for notation history, derivative language, and teachability of calculus.

access_routes.provider: Biodiversity Heritage Library via Internet Archive
access_routes.notes: Digitized volume of Acta Eruditorum containing the 1684 article.
Context route to the journal in which the article appeared.

sources.title: Pascal and Fermat correspondence on games of chance
sources.date_label: 1654 correspondence
sources.significance: Foundational story for fair division, expectation, and probability reasoning.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Critical for probability as method born from concrete problem correspondence.

access_routes.notes: Public course route pointing to translated teaching material on the correspondence.

sources.title: Apollonius: Conics
sources.date_label: 3rd century BCE original; extant through Greek, Arabic, and later print traditions
sources.significance: Canonical source for conic sections and a major bridge from Greek geometry to early modern analysis and astronomy.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Essential for the historical story of ellipse, parabola, hyperbola, and geometric problem style.

access_routes.notes: Public reading route for a historical edition of Conics with download options.
Route to the later Arabic transmission of Books V to VII.

sources.title: Diophantus: Arithmetica
sources.date_label: likely 3rd century CE; surviving through Greek and Arabic transmission
sources.significance: Central source for algebraic problem culture and later number-theoretic reception.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the history of indeterminate problems and algebraic problem-solving style.

access_routes.notes: Public edition of the six arithmetic books and polygonal numbers with download options.
Heath study with extensive historical apparatus around Arithmetica.

sources.title: Bhaskara II: Lilavati
sources.significance: Major arithmetic and mensuration text in the Indian mathematical tradition with very long teaching influence.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for worked arithmetic culture, verse mathematics, and transmission into later commentarial traditions.

access_routes.notes: Colebrooke translation volume containing Bhaskara material with download options.
Dedicated Lilavati edition hub for library or later acquisition.

sources.title: Bhaskara II: Bijaganita
sources.significance: Key algebra text for the Indian tradition and a major bridge after Brahmagupta.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for equation handling, algebraic procedures, and continuity toward later Indian and Kerala traditions.

access_routes.notes: Colebrooke translation volume gives a practical public-domain reading route.
Dedicated Bijaganita translation route through library holdings.

sources.title: Omar Khayyam: Demonstration concerning problems of algebra
sources.date_label: 11th to 12th century original; 1931 English translation route
sources.significance: Crucial source for cubic equations and their geometric solution before the early modern period.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important bridge between rhetorical algebra, conic methods, and later equation theory.

access_routes.notes: Snippet-access translation with table of contents and historical metadata.
Library route for the classic English translation by Daoud Kasir.

sources.title: Descartes: La Geometrie
sources.date_label: 1637 original; public-domain later editions available
sources.significance: Foundational for analytic geometry and the algebraization of geometric reasoning.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the shift from classical construction style to coordinate and algebraic representation.

access_routes.notes: Public-domain edition with download options.

sources.title: Cavalieri: Geometria indivisibilibus continuorum nova quadam ratione promota
sources.date_label: 1635, expanded 1653 editions
sources.significance: Seminal indivisibles text for the prehistory of integral calculus.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Critical for the story from Archimedean exhaustion to seventeenth-century infinitesimal techniques.

access_routes.notes: Full-view scan route for the 1653 edition.

sources.title: Wallis: Arithmetica infinitorum
sources.significance: One of the decisive bridge texts between indivisibles and later calculus.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for summation, quadrature, and the arithmetization of infinite processes.

access_routes.notes: Full-view historical scan route.

sources.title: Huygens: De Ratiociniis in Ludo Aleae
sources.significance: First printed book devoted to probability theory in the European tradition.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Essential bridge from Pascal-Fermat correspondence to systematic probability literature.

access_routes.notes: Full-view route for the 1657 treatise.

sources.title: Viete: In artem analyticam isagoge
sources.significance: Landmark text for symbolic algebra and the systematic use of letters for known and unknown quantities.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Essential for the transition from rhetorical algebra to symbolic manipulation that later supports modern equation practice.

access_routes.notes: Bibliographic route with full-view 1591 edition references and linked scans.

sources.title: Stevin: De Thiende
sources.significance: Canonical early modern text for decimal fractions and the push toward decimalized practical computation.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for notation history, arithmetic pedagogy, and the routinization of decimal representation.

access_routes.notes: Full-view route to the 1585 edition from the Dutch national library scan.
Author hub including locate-only facsimile listings for De Thiende.

sources.title: Napier: Mirifici logarithmorum canonis descriptio
sources.significance: Foundational publication of logarithms as a practical computational tool.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Essential for the history of calculation, tables, and the computational environment of early modern mathematics.

access_routes.notes: Direct scan route for the 1614 Descriptio.

sources.title: Jacob Bernoulli: Ars Conjectandi
sources.significance: Foundational bridge from early gambling problems to mature probability and combinatorics.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the law of large numbers tradition and the consolidation of probability as a field.

access_routes.notes: Modern scholarly translation and commentary route.

sources.title: Adelard of Bath: Euclid translation tradition
sources.date_label: 12th century
sources.significance: Major Latin transmission route carrying Euclidean geometry from Arabic scholarship into western Europe.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Essential for the story of how Euclidean proof culture became teachable in the Latin West.

access_routes.notes: Historical overview of Adelard's Euclid translation versions and their significance.
Heath edition with extensive historical commentary on medieval transmission.

sources.title: Campanus of Novara: Euclid tradition
sources.date_label: 13th century recension; influential in later print culture
sources.significance: The dominant later medieval Latin Euclid tradition and a key teaching route into Renaissance print culture.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for tracking how Euclidean propositions were presented to later European readers.

access_routes.notes: Heath route for commentary on Campanus and later medieval Euclid transmission.

sources.title: Heron: Metrica
sources.date_label: 1st century CE; recovered through later manuscript tradition
sources.significance: Key text for mensuration, area and volume formulas, and practical geometry.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the operational side of ancient geometry and the later teaching of measurement formulas.

access_routes.notes: Locate route for the Greek-English Brill edition.
Digitized historical edition route useful for bibliographic verification and partial reading.

sources.title: Pappus: Collection
sources.date_label: 4th century CE; surviving through later manuscript and print traditions
sources.significance: Major late antique synthesis of Greek mathematics and a crucial transmission source.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the theorem of Pappus, analysis and synthesis methods, and the preservation of earlier Greek mathematics.

access_routes.notes: Public-domain Hultsch edition with PDF download.
Modern translation and commentary for the mathematically influential seventh book.

sources.title: Al-Karaji: Al-Fakhri
sources.date_label: around early 11th century; 1853 excerpt edition route
sources.significance: One of the central algebra texts in the medieval Islamic tradition and a major step away from purely geometric algebra.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for polynomial operations, powers, and the development of algebraic procedure.

access_routes.notes: Full-view Woepcke edition of an algebra extract from al-Fakhri.
Direct PDF route for the same 1853 excerpt edition.

sources.title: Nicole Oresme: Tractatus de configurationibus qualitatum et motuum
sources.date_label: 14th century; modern bilingual edition route 1968
sources.significance: Crucial medieval work for quantified qualities, graphical thinking, and proto-functional reasoning.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the prehistory of coordinates, changing intensities, and analysis-style reasoning.

access_routes.notes: Locate route for the standard Clagett edition with Latin and English.
Snippet route for bibliographic confirmation and limited content preview.

sources.title: Regiomontanus: De triangulis omnimodis
sources.date_label: written 1464, printed 1533
sources.significance: Foundational European trigonometry text linking medieval astronomy and later mathematical practice.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Essential for systematic plane and spherical trigonometry before the calculus era.

access_routes.notes: Full-view scan of the 1533 printed edition.
Modern English translation route with bibliographic preview.

sources.title: Kepler: Astronomia nova
sources.significance: Major bridge between geometry, astronomy, physical reasoning, and infinitesimal-style thinking.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for ellipse-based planetary models and the path from geometric astronomy toward calculus-era methods.

access_routes.notes: Original 1609 Latin edition with download options.
Modern English translation route useful for teaching and verification.

sources.title: Fermat: Methodus ad disquirendam maximam et minimam
sources.date_label: 17th century; preserved in the 1679 Varia opera mathematica
sources.significance: One of the strongest pre-calculus routes to maxima, minima, and tangent-style reasoning.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the differential prehistory and Fermat's method of adequality.

access_routes.notes: Digital route to the 1679 collected edition containing the relevant Fermat texts.
Free digitized access to the same 1679 Varia opera mathematica.

sources.title: Barrow: Lectiones geometricae
sources.significance: Major conceptual and didactic bridge between seventeenth-century geometry and Newtonian calculus.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for tangent-area relations and the conceptual path toward the fundamental theorem tradition.

access_routes.notes: Open scan of the 1674 volume that includes Lectiones geometricae.
Collected works route with downloadable nineteenth-century reprint.

sources.title: Theon of Alexandria: Euclid and Ptolemy commentary tradition
sources.date_label: 4th century CE
sources.significance: Major late antique commentary route through which Euclid and mathematical astronomy were transmitted onward.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the survival, framing, and pedagogical ordering of classical mathematical argument.

access_routes.notes: Biographical route summarizing Theon's editorial and commentary role.
Heath edition route useful for tracing Theon's recension and its later reception.

sources.title: Hypatia: commentary tradition on Arithmetica and Conics
sources.date_label: late 4th to early 5th century CE
sources.significance: Key witness to high-level late antique mathematical commentary and extension work on major Greek texts.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for understanding how Diophantine and conic traditions remained mathematically active through commentary.

access_routes.notes: Biographical route summarizing Hypatia's mathematical commentary tradition.
Reference PDF with historical detail useful for metadata and transmission notes.

sources.title: Eutocius of Ascalon: commentaries on Archimedes and Apollonius
sources.date_label: 6th century CE
sources.significance: Crucial late antique preservation and explanatory route for Archimedean and Apollonian mathematics.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the textual survival and explicated proof structure of major Greek geometry works.

access_routes.notes: Biographical route covering Eutocius and his commentary corpus.
Collected Archimedes edition route for commentary-linked witness work.

sources.title: Aryabhata: Aryabhatiya
sources.date_label: 499 CE
sources.significance: Foundational Indian mathematics text spanning arithmetic, algebra, trigonometry, and astronomical computation.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for sine tables, numerical approximation, and the Indian line feeding later Islamic mathematics.

access_routes.notes: Library route for a standard English translation and edition.
Biographical route documenting Aryabhata's mathematical influence and transmission.

sources.title: Hipparchus: commentary and chord-table tradition
sources.date_label: 2nd century BCE; surviving through later commentary and witness traditions
sources.significance: Early anchor for trigonometric tabulation and geometric astronomy in the ancient world.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the prehistory of trigonometric tables later developed in Islamic and European mathematics.

access_routes.notes: Biographical route on Hipparchus and the origins of trigonometric practice.
Witness route for a surviving Hipparchus-linked text tradition.

sources.title: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi: Treatise on the Quadrilateral
sources.date_label: 13th century
sources.significance: Landmark work in separating trigonometry from astronomy and systematizing it as its own mathematical discipline.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for spherical trigonometry, triangle cases, and the sine-law lineage.

access_routes.notes: Biographical route covering al-Tusi's role in trigonometry and mathematical astronomy.
Library route for a modern edition or translation of the quadrilateral treatise.

sources.title: Henry Briggs: Arithmetica logarithmica
sources.significance: Operational breakthrough that made logarithms practically usable for large-scale scientific calculation.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the teachable shift from conceptual logarithm invention to standard computational tables.

access_routes.notes: Library route for the 1624 tables and later digitized copies.
Public scan route for a digitized copy of the work.

sources.title: Gregory of Saint-Vincent: Opus geometricum
sources.significance: Important bridge between quadrature problems, the hyperbola, and the later analytic understanding of logarithmic behavior.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for linking indivisibles-style area reasoning to the emerging function story around logarithms.

access_routes.notes: Full-view scan of the original work.
Biographical route describing Gregory's quadrature work and its historical role.

sources.title: Weierstrass: Mathematische Werke
sources.date_label: 1894 onward collected edition of nineteenth-century analysis work
sources.significance: Major access route to the work that reshaped rigorous analysis, convergence, and analytic function theory.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the later teachable lineage of epsilon-delta rigor, convergence criteria, and analytic function methods.

access_routes.notes: Biographical route summarizing Weierstrass and the lecture and publication tradition behind modern analysis.
Public-domain collected works route with downloadable scan access.

sources.title: Peano: Arithmetices principia, nova methodo exposita
sources.significance: Seminal foundation text for arithmetic axiomatization and formal symbolic language.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for explicit arithmetic axioms, formal notation, and the later foundations of mathematical logic.

access_routes.notes: Full-text route for the 1889 book with chapter-level access.
Biographical route for Peano's foundations work and symbolic logic role.

sources.title: Zermelo: Untersuchungen ueber die Grundlagen der Mengenlehre I
sources.significance: Foundational article for axiomatic set theory and the modern handling of choice and paradox-sensitive foundations.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for explicit axioms, set-theoretic formalization, and the foundations line after Cantor and Dedekind.

access_routes.notes: Open route to the 1908 Mathematische Annalen article.
Biographical route covering Zermelo's foundations work and axiomatic set theory.

sources.title: Hausdorff: Grundzuege der Mengenlehre
sources.significance: Landmark synthesis of set theory, topology, and metric-space thinking in the early twentieth century.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the teachable transition from set theory to topological and metric structure.

access_routes.notes: Public-domain scan route for the 1914 edition.
Biographical route explaining the book's role in topology and set theory.

sources.title: Hilbert and Ackermann: Grundzuege der theoretischen Logik
sources.significance: Important bridge from axiomatic ambitions in geometry and arithmetic to formal logic and proof theory.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for symbolic logic, decision problems, and the foundations background against which later incompleteness results were read.

access_routes.notes: Full-view route for the 1928 edition.
Review hub covering Hilbert's books, including the logic text written with Ackermann.

sources.title: Godel: Ueber formal unentscheidbare Saetze der Principia Mathematica und verwandter Systeme I
sources.significance: Foundational twentieth-century result showing essential limits of axiomatic formal systems.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for incompleteness, formal provability, and the conceptual background of computability and metamathematics.

access_routes.notes: Internet Archive-backed route to the standard English translation of the 1931 paper.
Biographical route summarizing the incompleteness theorems and their place in foundations.

sources.title: Abel: Memoire sur les equations algebriques, ou l'on demontre l'impossibilite de la resolution de l'equation generale du cinquieme degre
sources.date_label: 1824; collected in later editions of Abel's works
sources.significance: Foundational modern result on the insolvability of the general quintic and a major bridge from classical equations to structural algebra.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the transition from equation-solving ambition to algebraic impossibility and later group-theoretic understanding.

access_routes.notes: Public-domain collected works route containing Abel's major papers on equations and functions.
Biographical route summarizing Abel's equations work and its later importance.

sources.title: Kronecker: Werke
sources.date_label: 1895 onward collected edition of nineteenth-century work
sources.significance: Key access route to Kronecker's work on equations, algebraic numbers, and finitist-leaning foundations.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the arithmetic and constructivist counterpoint to Cantor, Dedekind, and later set-theoretic foundations.

access_routes.notes: Public-domain collected works route with downloadable scan access.
Biographical route for Kronecker's contributions to equations, algebraic numbers, and constructive viewpoints.

sources.title: Cayley: The collected mathematical papers of Arthur Cayley
sources.date_label: 1889 onward collected edition of nineteenth-century work
sources.significance: Central route to Cayley's work on matrices, invariant theory, abstract groups, and higher-dimensional geometry.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the emergence of abstract algebraic structure and matrix language before twentieth-century axiomatization.

access_routes.notes: Public-domain collected papers route with PDF and text download options.
Biographical route covering Cayley's work on matrices, groups, and geometry.

sources.title: Hamilton: Elements of Quaternions
sources.significance: Foundational work on quaternions and one of the major expansions of algebra beyond commutative arithmetic.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for non-commutative algebra, algebraic structure, and later links to geometry and physics.

access_routes.notes: Public-domain reading route for the original work and later editions.
Dedicated MacTutor route to Hamilton's quaternion text with historical framing.

sources.title: Klein: Vergleichende Betrachtungen ueber neuere geometrische Forschungen
sources.significance: Landmark text that recast geometry through transformation groups and invariants.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for the structural unification of geometries and the role of symmetry in modern mathematics.

access_routes.notes: Public-domain route to the 1872 Erlangen program text.
Biographical route explaining the Erlangen program and Klein's group-based view of geometry.

sources.title: Russell and Whitehead: Principia Mathematica
sources.significance: Major logicist attempt to reconstruct mathematics on symbolic logical foundations.
sources.proof_or_equation_value: Important for type theory, formal logical method, and the foundations debates later challenged by incompleteness.

access_routes.notes: Open scan route to the first volume of Principia Mathematica.
Biographical route covering Russell's logicism and the Principia project.
